notes: The 1985 report-section VALUE clause is the one-operand form 'VALUE IS literal-1' (§1985:XIII.3.22.2; function 'The VALUE clause defines the value of Report Section printable items', §1985:XIII.3.22.1). BindReportEntry routes a report VALUE through DataBinder.CheckValueConnective with pairedConnective: true (the 2023 format 4 'VALUE IS | VALUES ARE' choice) and has no edition arm, so at --std 85 'VALUES ARE "HELLO"' and bare 'VALUES "HELLO"' compile and run; the rest of the format is enforced at 85. Probes (work-rr-04): b) identifier operand (witness) COBOL1639, FUNCTION operand COBOL1902, two literals COBOL2012 via ScreenRepeatingOperandCount, VALUE written twice COBOL2423, empty 'VALUE IS.' COBOL0001; c) '&' concatenation and X"41" COBOL0900, N"AB" COBOL0898, OCCURS in a report entry COBOL0900, a group VALUE COBOL2247/COBOL0900; d) 'VALUE IS "HELLO"', S99 VALUE -12, 9(3) VALUE ZERO, X(4) VALUE ALL "*", X(3) VALUE SPACES and ZZ9.99 VALUE " 12.50" print 'HELLO    1K   000  ****       12.50'; SR2 range/size COBOL1625/COBOL1740. Classes a, e, f do not reach a VALUE IS literal-1 format. Only the VALUES spelling is under-rejected. kb/Work PB5242 holds the defect (code read: coderead-85/out-reread2/rr-04.json).

next.reason: 1985 Report Writer VALUE clause is only 'VALUE IS literal-1' (§1985:XIII.3.22.2). 2023 report-section Format 4 is '{VALUE IS | VALUES ARE} {literal-1} ...' (§2023:13.18.63.2); 'The words VALUE and VALUES are equivalent' (§2023:13.18.63.3 SR17, applied to the report format by §2023:13.18.63.3 SR34), and more than one operand is allowed in a repeating entry (§2023:13.18.63.3 SR35). Every 1985 form keeps its meaning; 2023 accepts VALUES ARE and several literals, which the 1985 format refuses (looser). 1985 VI.5.15.2's VALUES ARE is the condition-name format only, so no 1985 rule already allows this in a report item.
